title: Parking on large conditioned critical Galton–Watson trees with aperiodic finite-variance offspring and finite-variance arrivals of mean at most one has the moment-determined subcritical, critical and linear-flux phase transition
author: Nicolas Curien and Olivier Hénard
difficulty_reason: After the stated conditioned-tree local/fringe limits, classical spine identity and Wald hitting-time formula, one still has to derive the arrival-time integral equation and rule out premature explosion by finite-height monotone truncations. The main conditioned-tree conclusion additionally requires the explicit three-piece comparison and a locality argument absorbing both upper fluxes into empty lower-spine spots. Those source-local coupled constructions and limit controls are nonroutine, so the full theorem is conservatively H1.
work: The Phase Transition for Parking on Galton--Watson Trees

source_check.note: Only original Theorem 1, all three rows and all three regimes, under the exact aperiodic critical finite-variance offspring and independent finite-variance arrivals with positive mean at most one; both distributions differ from delta at 1. Ordinary prerequisites are Lyons--Peres Chapter 12.1 spinal identity; Janson [10, Theorem 1.3, quenched (1.11)] fringe convergence; Kortchemski--Richier [12, Eq. (12)] uniform height local limit; standard conditioned Galton--Watson local/scaling limits, Skorokhod embedding, random-walk hitting times/Wald and elementary continuous integral comparison. Every source-local rough comparison, arrival-time decomposition, truncation estimate and locality proof is included. The authors call the last continuous comparison at source 424 an easy exercise, after explicitly deriving its full integral inequality and continuity; this remains an ordinary comparison prerequisite, without an assistant-written argument. Literal source quirks such as the tree expectation sums at 299/301/343, the height-truncation bound mtn at 414 and final almost-sure closing at 498 are preserved without a mathematical verdict or repair.
